title: Negative lead-time values in balance.json `warnings` pass the 'leads > 0' fail-fast via u64 coercion wrap
evidence: core/catalog.odin:532-534 — "b.warnings.node_strained_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "node_strained_lead_ticks", 0))" / "b.warnings.node_critical_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "node_critical_lead_ticks", 0))" / "b.warnings.pipe_pressure_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "pipe_pressure_lead_ticks", 0))"; core/catalog.odin:541-543 — "if b.warnings.node_strained_lead_ticks == 0 || b.warnings.node_critical_lead_ticks == 0 ||" / "	b.warnings.pipe_pressure_lead_ticks == 0 {" / "	return {"balance.json", "warnings", "lead times must be > 0 (the FORGE #3 reaction-window surface)}""; precedent at core/catalog.odin:463-465 — "// tick fields are validated as i32 BEFORE the u64 casts — a" / "// negative JSON value must reject, never wrap to ~2^64 (the" / "// surge would silently never fire)." / "if mult < 1 || st < 0 || dt < 1 || fl < 0 {"
detail: The spec's fail-fast row requires 'a lead ≤ 0 → load aborts with a named error'. A negative JSON lead wraps through u64(jint(...)) to ~2^64 and passes the == 0 check — the boundary validation is defeated by coercion order, exactly the class the demand.json set-piece parse (same file, lines 463-465) was hardened against.
recommended_fix: Read each lead into an i32 local and reject lead < 0 (or == 0) BEFORE the u64 cast, mirroring the set-piece parse at catalog.odin:463-465; add negative-lead rows to catalog_test.
